reasons: Deviation classification is correct: the original clause is a one-way non-solicit binding only the Licensee (our party), runs for the Term plus three years (>24 months) and covers any person employed by Licensor or its Affiliates — two material failures of the fallback and squarely in the rule's walk-away territory.

The redline reaches the fallback with targeted edits: mutuality, scope limited to personnel directly involved in the performance/receipt of the services, and a 12-month tail measured from the end of that involvement, while leaving the existing general-advertising and voluntary-inquiry carve-outs intact. No no-hire language was introduced.

The failed deterministic duration check is a phrasing artifact — the redline expressly states 'twelve (12) month period following the end of an individual's involvement', which satisfies the fallback duration; the 0.594 changed-character ratio is justified because duration, scope and mutuality all had to be rewritten in a single sentence.
Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice, explains what changed and cites the playbook position (no restraints >24 months or covering an entire counterparty workforce) without lecturing.
Direction of change favours our party (narrows the restraint on Customer and adds reciprocity), and the finding does not duplicate another rule's commercial term.
